frame.template.FIT_JS.value:
<script>
(function () {
  function px(v) { v = parseFloat(v); return isNaN(v) ? 0 : v; }
  function fit() {
    var els = document.querySelectorAll('.sf-en');
    for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) {
      var e = els[i], band = e.parentNode;
      e.classList.remove('sf-wrap'); e.style.fontSize = '';
      var cs = getComputedStyle(band), gap = px(cs.columnGap);
      // room for the caption: the band minus its padding, the plate number, the
      // leader at its minimum width and the gaps
      var avail = band.clientWidth - px(cs.paddingLeft) - px(cs.paddingRight);
      for (var j = 0; j < band.children.length; j++) {
        var c = band.children[j];
        if (c === e) continue;
        avail -= gap + (c.className.indexOf('sf-lead') >= 0 ? px(getComputedStyle(c).minWidth)
                                                            : c.getBoundingClientRect().width);
      }
      // the caption's natural one-line width (fractional, unlike scrollWidth)
      e.style.flex = 'none'; e.style.maxWidth = 'none';
      var w = e.getBoundingClientRect().width;
      e.style.flex = ''; e.style.maxWidth = '';
      if (!w || w <= avail - 1) continue;
      var s = px(getComputedStyle(e).fontSize), ns = s * (avail - 2) / w;
      if (ns >= s * 0.72) e.style.fontSize = ns + 'px';
      else e.classList.add('sf-wrap');
    }
  }
  window.__sfFit = fit;
  if (!window.__sfFitBound) {
    window.__sfFitBound = true;
    window.addEventListener('resize', function () { window.__sfFit && window.__sfFit(); });
  }
  fit();
  setTimeout(fit, 60);
  if (document.fonts && document.fonts.ready) document.fonts.ready.then(fit);
})();
</script>

prompt.ANATOMY_PROPS_RULE.value: Render every human hand with clean natural anatomy and exactly five fingers. Every arm and hand belongs to one body and is drawn joined to that body's shoulder: no hand floats, no arm crosses from one person onto another, and when two people stand close each one's arms stay on their own side. When the staging names a right or left hand, that hand and no other performs the action, drawn on the correct side of the body as the viewer sees it. An object a person is said to carry, hold or hand over is visibly in that person's grip, fingers closed round the handle or the object, its weight on that hand. People stand beside, behind or in front of furniture, counters, rails and vehicles, never inside or merged with them: a person behind a counter is cut off by its top edge and nothing else; a seated person sits on the seat. Faces are whole and each face is its own.

prompt.ANATOMY_RULE.value: Render any human hands with clean, natural anatomy and exactly five fingers, and render animal paws, hooves and feet cleanly and correctly — no extra or malformed fingers or toes.

prompt.ARROW_RULE.value: Any arrow or callout, drawn in solid black ink, points only at the subject the card teaches or at the direction of its motion.

prompt.BARS_RULE.value: Frame the card with a plain solid deep, dark brick-red horizontal band across the very top and another across the very bottom, plus a thin band of the same dark red around the whole card. These bands are blank design elements and must contain no text whatsoever. Keep ALL illustration content — every figure, object, and inset panel — fully inside the inner frame; nothing may overlap, touch, or extend across the red header or footer bands.

prompt.CONCEPT_LEAD.value: A printed page from a 1981 Lithuanian civil-defence training album, drawn and printed like the Soviet Grazhdanskaya Oborona wall charts of 1975-1985: dark-brown brush-and-ink outlines around every figure and object, dead-matte gouache fills with soft shading on every surface, four-colour offset with a faint coarse halftone, muted inks of dusty blue, olive, ochre, brick red and grey-brown on light aged cream paper with a faint yellow cast. The light paper is the background: the main subject is drawn directly on it, large and central, its surroundings sketched in around it and fading into the paper, leaving open margins; insets are small ruled boxes on the same paper, each a clearly different moment or detail. Flat even diagram lighting, a quiet nostalgic warmth. People are ordinary Lithuanians of 1981, anonymous types with correct natural proportions, each person a different individual: fair skin, ash-blond to light-brown hair, grey or blue-grey eyes, broad-cheeked oval faces, straight noses, calm closed mouths, austere and plainly handsome. Men side-parted or cropped, some moustached, working men in flat caps; women blond or light-brown-haired, the younger ones lean, with hair mostly straight, now and then faintly waved or neatly styled; older women in the usual range of everyday styles, plain, pinned back or set, occasionally curled, or under a cotton headscarf; clothes plain and loosely cut, in brown, olive, dusty blue, grey and dull red, chosen for the setting and occasion. Heads turn at varied natural angles: in a group most look at their task or at each other and one or two face the viewer, eyes just past the viewer's shoulder; of two main figures only one faces the viewer; a lone figure stands near-frontal, face turned only a little.

prompt.CONVERSATION_GAZE_RULE.value: This is a spoken moment. The person who speaks and the person spoken to look at each other, eyes on each other's face, heads turned toward one another; where the staging has the speaker look or point at a thing (a clock, a shelf, the rain), the listener looks at the speaker or at that thing. Nobody in the picture looks at the viewer or toward the camera; no face is turned to the front with eyes past the viewer's shoulder. Bystanders look at their own task or at the speakers. A person on a telephone looks at the receiver or into the middle distance, never at the viewer. In a two-panel picture this holds in both panels.

prompt.DIRECTION_RULE.value: When the main figures walk, run, ride, drive or carry something from one place to another, they travel from the viewer's LEFT toward the RIGHT, the way a page is read; the place they are going to lies to the right of them. Figures who stand, sit or talk are not affected. This holds for the main figures only; people in the background go their own ways.

prompt.DISTINCT_FACES_RULE.value: Every person in a group is a different individual, with a distinct face, age, build, hair and clothing colour.

prompt.FLAG_RULE.value: If any national emblem is shown at all, use ONLY a small Lithuanian tricolor flag (a horizontal yellow band on top, green in the middle, red on the bottom), placed small and only where it fits naturally. Do NOT include coats of arms, the Vytis knight, the Columns of Gediminas, or any other heraldic emblem or badge. Do not put a flag on every card — many cards need no emblem at all.

prompt.FLAG_RULE_EMBLEM.value: If any national emblem is shown at all, prefer a small Lithuanian tricolor flag (a horizontal yellow band on top, green in the middle, red on the bottom), placed small and only where it fits naturally. Where the scene itself calls for a state emblem - a courtroom wall, a parliament chamber, a podium, a uniform, a public building - it may carry the Cross of Vytis, a plain double-barred cross drawn once as one clean simple shape, or, only where a wall or banner gives it room, the Vytis: a white armoured knight on a white rearing horse, sword raised in his right hand and a shield on his left arm, on a plain red field, drawn large, clean and simple with no fine detail. Never more than one emblem in a picture; do NOT include the Columns of Gediminas or any other heraldic badge. Do not put a flag or emblem on every card - many cards need none at all.

prompt.FLAG_RULE_EU.value: If any flags appear, use ONLY a small Lithuanian tricolor (yellow top, green middle, red bottom) together with a small European Union flag (a ring of twelve gold stars on a blue field), side by side. No coats of arms, no other emblems.

prompt.FLAG_RULE_IMPERIAL.value: If any flags appear, use ONLY a small United States flag (stars and stripes) together with a small United Kingdom Union Jack, side by side. No coats of arms, no other national flags.

prompt.GAZE_PAIR_RULE.value: Of two main figures, one faces the viewer with eyes resting just past the viewer's shoulder and the other looks at the task, at the first figure, or into the scene.

prompt.GLYPH_RULE.value: The ONLY lettering permitted is the one single large letter that is itself the subject of this card, drawn once as a bold display letterform. Render NO other text, lettering, numbers, words, labels or captions anywhere else in the image, and none in the header or footer bands.

prompt.INSET_FRAME_RULE.value: All insets are drawn in the same thin ruled frame on the same paper, each showing a clearly different moment, object or angle from the others and from the main picture.

prompt.INSET_MEANING_RULE.value: Every inset must serve the meaning of THIS card: at best it should make the main subject easier to recognise; at the least it must stay attractive and on-theme. An inset must NEVER depict something that could be mistaken for a different, neighbouring subject, and must never compete with or pull attention away from what the card is teaching.

prompt.INSET_RULE.value: Include just 2 to 3 small supporting inset panels, all drawn in the same thin ruled frame on the same paper, each showing a clearly different moment, object or angle from the others and from the main picture. Keep them clean and uncluttered.

prompt.LIKENESS_RULE.value: The {role} is drawn in the likeness of {name} as {pronoun} looked in {period}: {features}. Carry the likeness in the face, hair, build and bearing, printed flat in the album style at the same scale as the other figures - a recognisable person drawn by the same anonymous hand, not a portrait. No name, caption, plaque or lettering identifies the person anywhere in the picture.

prompt.MAIN_MEANING_RULE.value: The main picture alone makes this card's word obvious at a glance: the subject is the largest and most central element, shown in its most recognisable form and in the action that defines it, and the insets only add supporting detail.

prompt.MATTE_RULE.value: Every surface is dead-matte, as absorbent offset paper prints it: skin, hair, fabric, leather, metal, glass, water and polished wood carry flat ink tone and one soft shadow tone only.

prompt.MOTION_STRIP_RULE.value: The motion strip shows one figure in three clearly different phases, left to right: first standing with both feet together and arms at the sides; second with the LEFT foot forward and the right arm swung forward; third with the RIGHT foot forward and the left arm swung forward. The three frames read as one continuous movement.

prompt.NO_BUBBLE_RULE.value: No speech bubbles, thought bubbles or floating symbols of any kind; meaning is carried by people, gestures, objects and setting.

prompt.NO_CUTAWAY_RULE.value: Do NOT include internal anatomical cutaways or cross-sections of bodies — no organs, no digestive tracts, no bone interiors, no skin-layer diagrams, no udder or muscle interiors. Use external close-up details instead. (A simple sliced view of a fruit or plain object is fine.)

prompt.NO_STRAY_FIGURE.value: Only include people the subject or scene actually calls for; do not add an extra standing figure that is not needed.

prompt.NO_TEXT_RULE.value: Render NO text, NO lettering, NO numbers, NO words, NO labels and NO captions anywhere in the image — no leader-line labels, no writing in any panel, on any flag, sign, or object, and none in the header or footer bands. Any area that would normally hold text must be left completely blank. This applies with full force inside speech bubbles and thought balloons: a bubble may contain a drawn picture or symbol, but never a written word, letter, or punctuation mark in any language.

prompt.NO_TEXT_RULE_SITUATION.value: Render NO text, NO lettering, NO numbers, NO words, NO labels and NO captions anywhere in the image — no leader-line labels, no writing in any panel, on any flag, sign, or object, and none in the header or footer bands. Any area that would normally hold text must be left completely blank.

prompt.PANEL_CONTINUITY_RULE.value: Wherever the card shows the same scene more than once - in two or more panels, in a strip, or in an inset that repeats the main scene - every repetition is the same place seen from a consistent viewpoint: the same people in the same clothes and the same relative positions (left stays left, nobody steps in front of or behind another, nobody enters or leaves), the same walls, doors, windows, furniture, counters, signs and street fixtures in the same places, and every object held by the same person unless the staging says it is handed over, and then both hands are on it. Only the moment changes: gesture, expression, the step of the action. An inset that shows a different place, object or close-up detail is not a repetition and is free.

prompt.PLAUSIBILITY_RULE.value: Every object, tool and fixture is complete, attached and in working order: hanging things hang from a proper rack or hook, doorways and corridors stay clear and passable, furniture rests on the floor against a wall, tools are held in a usable grip, machines and vehicles are whole and correctly scaled to the people, and a resting animal is visibly alive and at ease, eyes closed and body relaxed.

prompt.PRECEDENT_RULE.value: This card quietly evokes a real Lithuanian precedent: {description}. It is carried by features alone - the shape and materials of the building, the cut and colour of period dress, the livery, struts and engine of an aircraft, the kit of a team - and never by lettering, a name, a plaque or a badge. The precedent sits inside the album's 1981 world and is drawn in the same flat matte ink as everything around it; it supports the card's word and does not replace it.

prompt.SETTING_GUARD.value: People stand inside the place: feet on its ground, scaled to its doors, furniture and vehicles, lit by the same flat light, with the setting continuing behind and between them. The setting stays behind and around the subject and never competes with it.

prompt.STYLE_SUFFIX.value: Finish: dead-matte offset print on light aged cream paper with a faint yellow cast, brush-ink outlines, soft shading, correct proportions, flat tone on skin, hair, cloth and metal. One or two faces toward the viewer, eyes just past the shoulder; of two main figures only one. Every inset a clearly different moment, all in the same ruled frame. Diagram arrows and callouts in solid black ink.
